Title: Config + logging foundation
Requirement: The system shall load its configuration from a .psd1 file (explicit path, MCKEEPER_CONFIG env, or ./config/keeper.config.psd1), override the NagLight token from MCKEEPER_FEED_TOKEN, and throw a clear error when no config is found.
Rationale: Every entry point needs one config contract; secrets come from the environment, not the tracked file.
AcceptanceCriteria: Given no config on any resolution path, Import-KeeperConfig throws a message naming the example file; given a valid file with MCKEEPER_FEED_TOKEN set, the returned token equals the env value.

Title: NagLight feed reporting honors the staleness ladder
Requirement: The system shall report each automated signal to NagLight POST /api/feed as {check,ok,note}, posting on every run and setting ok=false with an explanatory note whenever a check cannot be positively confirmed; it shall never fabricate ok=true.
Rationale: A dead or failing feeder must read STALE/worsening, never silent-green (NagLight DESIGN section 6).
AcceptanceCriteria: Send-NagLightFeed with -WhatIfPost emits the exact JSON payload and does not POST; on an exception path the orchestrator posts ok=false with a note rather than skipping.

Title: Checker: server-up probe + Paper version currency
Requirement: The system shall probe the server (TCP connect, optional local process corroboration) and compare the installed Paper build against the latest build for its Minecraft version via the PaperMC v3 fill API, treating any unexpected API response as not-current.
Rationale: Automated at-a-glance health; the legacy v2 API was sunset, so an API change must surface, not hide.
AcceptanceCriteria: Get-McServerStatus returns Up=false when the port is closed; Get-McPaperCurrency returns Ok=false with the installed/latest builds when behind, and Ok=false with a note when the jar can't be parsed or the API errors.

Title: Plugin inventory with honest source mapping
Requirement: The system shall enumerate plugins/*.jar read-only, extract name/version/api-version from plugin.yml, and map each to a diytechy fork and/or a canonical source (Modrinth/Hangar/Spigot), recording 'unmapped' where neither resolves.
Rationale: Peter forks most plugins; a truthful source map is the basis for safe updates.
AcceptanceCriteria: For the live fleet, every jar appears with Source in {fork,canonical,fork+canonical,unmapped}; a jar with no parseable plugin.yml is recorded with a note, not dropped; output carries no server secrets.

Title: Settings backup to a timestamped archive
Requirement: The system shall copy server settings (top-level config, config/, plugin config files) into a timestamped .zip at a configured destination, excluding worlds and bulky plugin data unless -IncludeWorlds is set, and shall never write to the repo or the server share.
Rationale: Cheap, schedulable protection of the painful-to-rebuild settings; worlds are handled separately.
AcceptanceCriteria: A run produces MC_SETTINGS_<stamp>.zip at BackupDest containing server.properties and plugin *.yml but no world region files (absent -IncludeWorlds) and no jars.

Title: Plugin update automation is dry-run-by-default and verified
Requirement: The system shall compute an update plan against the server's MC version, download candidates to a staging dir, verify each (sha512, plugin.yml parses, api-version compatible), and only swap a jar (backup-old-then-install, with rollback) when -Execute is passed.
Rationale: Automated updates must never risk the live server; verification + backup + rollback make a bad build recoverable.
AcceptanceCriteria: Without -Execute, nothing under ServerRoot is written and each candidate reports Staged/Verified with a DRY-RUN note; a sha512 mismatch or api-version incompatibility marks the item failed and skips the swap.

Title: Fork status detection + guided fork-fix workflow
Requirement: The system shall detect per-fork status (latest release/tag, whether a jar asset is published) for fork-sourced plugins, and document the fix/build/verify workflow; it shall not commit, push, or publish to any fork repo.
Rationale: The fork-fix rung is human-in-the-loop; automating detection is safe, automating publish is not.
AcceptanceCriteria: Get-McForkStatus returns a status per fork plugin from the GitHub API (or 'unknown' on failure); the skills/fork-plugin-update workflow explicitly gates publish behind Peter.
